title: Finding Fulfillment: Joy, Skill, Need and the three traps that cause burnout
summary: Jason Cohen presents a framework for fulfillment at work: you need Joy, Skill, and Need together, and any two without the third create a predictable trap (useless flow, indulgent failure, or burn-out). He used it to step aside as CEO of WP Engine and become CTO, and pairs it with Pink's motivation model and Sinek's "Start with Why."

principles.text: Fulfillment requires Joy, Skill and Need together; any two without the third creates a specific trap.
principles.quote: Not only do you need *all three* of the following components, but any two alone create a specific trap

principles.text: Joy plus Skill without Need is pleasant but unproductive flow, and founders often have nobody to tell them so.
principles.quote: there's no one willing or able to tell you to your face that you're not contributing to what the company needs, so you stay in your happy place.

principles.text: Joy plus Need without Skill leads founders to indulge in jobs they're bad at, wasting months and drawing wrong conclusions.
principles.quote: You might even erroneously conclude "AdWords doesn't work" because that's an easier conclusion than "I don't know what I'm doing."

principles.text: Skill plus Need without Joy is burn-out, hidden because great results make it look like no problem.
principles.quote: Because you create great results that the company needs, it doesn't look like a problem--not to you, nor your team.

principles.text: Don't hoard work you hate; someone else may enjoy it, and you're blocking them and yourself from being happier.
principles.quote: Some people actually *like* the thing you hate, and you're preventing them--and you--from being happier.

principles.text: Ego can keep founders in the CEO role even when it makes them unhappy; moving to the center of the Venn diagram served both the person and the company.
principles.quote: So it's hard to convince the ego to let go of being the CEO, as I did at WP Engine, even if being the CEO creates unhappiness.
